newsitem.title: USA: Tobacco deal needs study, possible revision - Gore.
newsitem.headline: Tobacco deal needs study, possible revision - Gore.

text.p: Vice President Al Gore on Monday said a $368.5 billion accord between U.S. states and the tobacco industry needed to be carefully studied and parts might have to be rewritten.

In an interview on CNN's "Larry King Live," Gore complimented state attorneys general and other negotiators on their "herculean" efforts, but he stressed "something this large needs careful scrutiny."

"There's a lot that appears to be good in it. (But) there are some features of it that give me pause for concern," he said. One such feature was limitations on the Food and Drug Administration's jurisdiction over tobacco, he said.

Tobacco companies on Friday agreed to pay $368.5 billion over 25 years, admit that tobacco is addictive, and accept extensive federal regulation over their products and advertising. In return, they would get immunity from further punitive liability for any past deception, fraud or conspiracy.
The White House on Monday said President Bill Clinton had formed eight working groups within the government to review the tobacco settlement and complete an analysis within 30 days.
Gore said the review would proceed very carefully, examining the entire package.

"Let's get the whole package out. Maybe we'll see that it's a starting point, and with some improvements -- who knows how extensive -- it could serve as the sort of solution the country's looking for," he said.
The interview was taped on Monday in Nashville, Tennessee, where Gore was preparing for a conference on families.
